{{Short description|German mathematician (1894–1968)}}
[[File:Hoheisel,Guido 1930 Jena.jpg|thumb|Guido Hoheisel (1930)]]
'''Guido Karl Heinrich Hoheisel''' (14 July 1894 – 11 October 1968) was a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics at the [[University of Cologne]].

== Academic life ==
He did his PhD in 1920 from the [[University of Berlin]] under the supervision of [[Erhard Schmidt]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=20710}}.</ref> 
During [[World War II]] Hoheisel was required to teach classes simultaneously at three universities, in [[Cologne]], [[Bonn]], and [[Münster]].<ref>{{citation|title=Mathematicians under the Nazis|first=Sanford L.|last=Segal|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2003|isbn=978-0-691-00451-8|page=210|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Xa8CNCyohBQC&pg=PA210}}.</ref> His doctoral students include [[Arnold Schönhage]].

Hoheisel contributed to the journal [[Deutsche Mathematik]].

== Selected results ==
Hoheisel is known for a result on [[gaps between prime numbers]]:<ref>G. Hoheisel, ''Primzahlprobleme in der Analysis'', Berliner Sitzungsberichte, pages 580-588, (1930)</ref> 
He proved that if π(x) denotes the [[prime-counting function]], then there exists a constant θ < 1 such that

:π(''x'' + ''x''<sup>θ</sup>) − π(''x'') ~ ''x''<sup>θ</sup>/log(''x''),

as ''x'' tends to infinity, implying that if ''p''<sub>''n''</sub> denotes the ''n''-th [[prime number]] then

:''p''<sub>''n''+1</sub> − ''p''<sub>''n''</sub> < ''p''<sub>''n''</sub><sup>''θ'',</sup>

for all [[sufficiently large]] ''n''. He showed that one may take 

:''θ = 32999/33000 = 1 - 0.000(03),'' 

with (03) denoting periodic repetition.
